title: Justifying Superpoly Assumptions in Division-Property Cube Attacks
summary: The source proposes strong and weak superpoly conditions for attack validity under a key-length restriction, but general guarantees for enough qualifying non-cube IV assignments remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For a division-property-based cube attack, let $C_I$ denote a cube of IV variables, let $J$ denote a set of key bits, and let $n$ be the key length. The attack uses the corresponding superpoly under assignments to the remaining, constant IV variables. Its validity is based on either a strong condition that many such assignments make the superpoly balanced or a weak condition that many make it nonconstant, with $|I|+|J|<n$. The unresolved task is to prove or characterize conditions guaranteeing that these many non-cube IV assignments exist, especially when $|I|+|J|$ is close to $n$, where the rationale for the assumptions is difficult to establish.

scope.domain: This concerns symmetric cryptanalysis of division-property-based cube attacks and their superpolies.
assumptions: Many assignments to the remaining constant IV variables make the corresponding superpoly balanced (strong condition).
Many assignments to the remaining constant IV variables make the corresponding superpoly nonconstant (weak condition).
The attack is considered under |I| + |J| < n.
parameters: Remaining constant IV variables: variables assigned outside the cube
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove or characterize conditions guaranteeing that many non-cube IV assignments yield balanced or nonconstant corresponding superpolies, especially when |I| + |J| is close to n.

citations.label: Improved Division Property Based Cube Attacks Exploiting Algebraic Properties of Superpoly

progress.summary: The source presents strong and weak assumptions as the basis for validating the attack under the key-length restriction. It says their rationality is difficult to prove, especially near the boundary; a flag technique offers only partial support in the studied attacks.
citation_labels: Qingju Wang et al., Improved Division Property Based Cube Attacks Exploiting Algebraic Properties of Superpoly
